transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I'm here because... well, things have gotten a bit complicated lately. I've started, um, planning my days around avoiding elevators. Like, I'll take the five flights of stairs at my apartment instead. I even turned down a workshop I was supposed to run because it was in a high-rise. And... I had to stop visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have another way up. So, yeah. That's why I'm here.
Can you tell me more about why you avoid elevators? What are you most concerned might happen if you use one?

I just... I don't know. I guess I'm afraid of getting stuck. Like, I know the elevators in big office buildings are supposed to be fine, but... when I look at the old doors in my apartment, or even the ones at work, my brain just... it just tells me I'm going to get trapped in there. Or that it's going to drop. I know it sounds stupid and over the top, but... I just can't do it.
Do you experience similar kinds of intense fears or avoidance with other things or situations, or is this mostly limited to elevators?
No, not really. It's... just elevators. I don't really have a problem with anything else.
How long have you felt this way about elevators? Has this fear been building up over time, or did it start suddenly?

Um... about seven months, I think. It started right after I moved into my current place. The one on the fifth floor. There was... an incident with the elevator. A scare, I guess. It's just been like this since then.
When you were stuck or had the scare in the elevator seven months ago, did you experience a sudden rush of intense fear or physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Yeah... I mean, during the scare, sure. But honestly, it's like that now, too. Just... if I even step toward one, or hear the doors clunk open... my chest gets tight. My hands get sweaty. It's just... this rush of panic. It hits me before I even really have time to think it through.
Have you ever experienced similar panic or intense anxiety in situations other than being near or using elevators?
Um... no. I don't think so. Just... just with the elevators. I don't really get like that anywhere else.
Have you ever had sudden panic attacks or extreme anxiety in situations that weren't related to elevators?
Um... no. Like I said, it's just the elevators. I don't really have that happen anywhere else.
Have you ever gone out of your way to avoid other situations or places because you were afraid of having a panic attack or feeling anxious, or is it mostly just elevators?
No... I don't avoid anything else. Just the elevators. That's really it.
Has the fear of elevators ever caused you to worry about it affecting your life in other ways, like being seen as irrational or making you feel embarrassed?
Not really. I mean... I don't really talk about it with anyone. I just take the stairs, so... it doesn't really come up. I don't think about it much beyond that.
Has this fear of elevators caused you significant distress or affected your ability to function in daily life, such as at work or in social situations?

I mean... I guess a little bit. It's not a huge deal, but... I did turn down a workshop assignment for my job recently because it was in a high-rise. And... I volunteer teaching computer skills to seniors, and I had to stop visiting one of the guys. His building basically requires taking the elevator. So... yeah, just those things.
